title: DASS: A Solver-Adaptable Dynamic Auxiliary Search Strategy for Symbolic Regression
claim: Unguided solvers wander the full search space; a closed loop of initializing, calibrating and reshaping a guiding subspace steers them to the target.
layout: 5 panels, left-to-right, unguided baseline panel beside highlighted 4-stage closed loop
description: A wide figure with two rounded containers. The small left one, titled "SR Solver Only: Search without guidance", shows an oval search space. A polyline of scattered nodes wanders around it and slowly nears a star target. Below it a dashed box lists LLM-, GP- and MCTS-based solvers with small icons. The large right container is titled "Solver-Adaptable Dynamic Auxiliary Search Strategy" and has four ovals: Subspace Initialization, Subspace Calibration, Search by SR Solver (highlighted in a green box), and Subspace Reshaping. Each oval has a green subspace ellipse that moves and shrinks toward the star. Bar charts of basis terms such as x(t)^3 and sin^2 t sit under three of the ovals. A "New" term appears in the last chart. Grey "Guide" arrows link the stages and form a feedback loop. Green upward arrows connect the labels (LLM Prior-Driven, Multi-Environment-Driven, Feedback-Driven) to the ovals. The eye goes first to the green highlighted solver panel.
caption: Core idea of DASS. Instead of letting an SR solver search the full expression space without guidance, DASS provides a solver-adaptable auxiliary search subspace spanned by high-potential basis terms. The subspace is initialized from LLM prior knowledge, calibrated by multi-environment evaluation, and reshaped using feedback from high-quality solver results. In this way, DASS guides diverse SR solvers toward promising regions while continuously refining the guided subspace.
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) aims to discover interpretable mathematical expressions from data and plays a key role in scientific discovery. However, existing methods face a common bottleneck: the enormous search space and severe combinatorial explosion make it difficult to achieve a favorable trade-off between accuracy and algorithmic efficiency. We argue that, in addition to designing increasingly complex solver-specific SR strategies, an equally promising direction is to equip them with a shareable auxiliary strategy that can provide reliable search guidance. To this end, we propose DASS, a solver-adaptable Dynamic Auxiliary Search Strategy that improves SR by constructing and refining a high-potential auxiliary search subspace. DASS represents the auxiliary search space as a functional subspace spanned by a set of high-potential basis function terms. It estimates term utility through multi-environment evaluation, filters unstable guidance, and updates term potential scores with a Gibbs posterior, thereby calibrating the subspace to provide more reliable guidance for downstream solvers. The high-quality solutions produced by the solver are used to update the set of basis terms. This forms a virtuous closed-loop optimization process: the subspace guides the downstream solver, and the solver feedback reshapes the subspace for subsequent exploration. DASS can be easily integrated with various types of SR solvers. Extensive experiments on LLM-SRBench show that DASS significantly improves the accuracy of original solvers with a manageable increase in runtime.
